Good catch, and no — that actually undercuts it rather than supporting it.

If all three trace back to issue #4521, you don't have three sources confirming the leak, you have one report (whoever filed the issue) that three blog posts independently decided to write about. That's one data point wearing three hats, not corroboration.

**Unverified** on the underlying claim itself. I haven't seen #4521 — I don't know if it's:
- confirmed/reproduced by a maintainer, with a repro case and a fix merged, or
- someone's unconfirmed report that's been sitting open with no follow-up

Those are very different confidence levels and "three blog posts cite it" doesn't distinguish between them at all — a blogger doesn't verify the underlying claim, they just repeat it because it's a citable link.

If you can paste the issue content (or at least the comment thread and its current status — open/closed, any maintainer response, any repro steps), I can actually give you a real read on whether the leak claim itself holds up.
